pageCache.text:
Headteacher's Welcome
On behalf of the children, staff, parents and governors at St Edmund’s Catholic Nursery and Primary School, I am delighted to welcome you to our community. We encourage children at our school to flourish and grow academically, personally and spiritually; we aim to develop and encourage the growth of the whole child.
From the ages of 3 through to 11, we provide a caring, vibrant and faith-filled environment where every child is known, valued and encouraged to shine. The moment you step through our doors, you will notice the joyful buzz of learning, the colourful displays of creativity, and the warm smiles that reflect our school’s family spirit. Parents consistently choose St Edmund’s as their local primary school of choice because of our welcoming atmosphere, excellent results and strong community.
Learning that Inspires For more than 85 years, St Edmund’s has delivered a rich and ambitious primary curriculum designed to spark imagination and build strong foundations for the future. Alongside English and Maths, children enjoy Sport, Art, Music, Drama, French and much more — discovering their talents and developing a lifelong love of learning. Our spacious grounds and exciting learning environment give children the freedom to explore, play and achieve their very best.
High Standards, Happy Children Our dedicated staff set high expectations while creating a safe environment and a supportive atmosphere. Ofsted 2022 describes St Edmund’s as “a happy community where pupils enjoy their learning, feel safe and rise to the challenges their teachers provide”.
In December 2024, the Catholic Schools Inspectorate awarded the school Outstanding status, praising the exceptional care and respect that underpin our children’s exemplary behaviour and attitudes.
Growing in Character and Confidence Beyond the classroom, pupils develop leadership and responsibility through our School Council, Eco Team, Mini Vinnies, Prefects, Buddies and Anti-Bullying Ambassadors. These opportunities build resilience, kindness and confidence, qualities that prepare them for life.
Enrichment and Achievement St Edmund’s pupils consistently achieve academic results above the national average. But their school journey is about much more: after-school clubs, sports competitions, trips, performances and outdoor learning all help broaden horizons and create lasting memories. We are proud holders of the Platinum School Games Award, reflecting our passion for sport and healthy lifestyles as well as the Music Mark in recognition of our high-quality music provision.
A Community that Welcomes All While rooted in our Catholic values; we warmly welcome families of all faiths and none. Together with parents and our parish, we create a strong partnership to ensure every child feels secure, supported and celebrated.We’d love to welcome you and your child to the St Edmund’s family; where faith, friendship and a love of learning grow hand in hand. We live our mission statement ‘Together we learn and grow through worship and celebration’ and warmly invite you to be part of this shared journey.
Mrs Carmel Moreland Headteacher

pageCache.text:
Catholic Life and Mission
At St Edmund’s, our Catholic identity is at the heart of everything we do. Christ is at the centre of our school community, guiding our words, actions, and relationships. Here, faith is not just taught but lived each day, helping children grow spiritually, morally, and academically in a nurturing environment.
Our mission statement, “Together we learn and grow through worship and celebration,” captures the essence of life at St Edmund’s. Through prayer, liturgy, religious education, and acts of service, pupils come to know God’s love and learn to share it with others.
We are proud to be a school where faith can flourish, where Gospel values shape daily life, and where children are encouraged to live with kindness, respect, and responsibility. Our Catholic ethos inspires us to serve our community and the wider world, ensuring that every child leaves St Edmund’s with both strong foundations for learning and a deep sense of faith and purpose.

Catholic Social Teaching
At St Edmund's we have been using the Caritas scheme of work to explain the principles of Catholic Social Teaching to our children. Catholic Social Teaching is a rich treasure of wisdom about building a just society and living lives of holiness amidst the challenges of modern society. It applies Gospel values like love, peace, justice, and service to social problems.
The scheme divides the principles into six areas, which include dignity, solidarity, the common good, and caring for creation. These are explained to the children and then we try to capture how we, as Christians, can live out these principals at St Edmund's School. These range from being an Eco-Rep to a Mini-Vinnie, from raising money for a specific charity to closing the doors to save heat, from being kind to our friends and speaking respectfully to looking after the plant around the school. The children understand that we behave in these ways because God has asked us to and we want to respond to his call.

Church Ministries
Guild of St Stephen: Altar Servers Ministry
The Guild of St Stephen is an International Organisation of Altar Servers founded in England in 1904 by Father Hamilton McDonald when he formed a Society of Altar Servers at the Convent of the Sacred Heart in London.
In 1905, Pope Pius X gave his approbation to the Canonical establishment of the Guild at Westminster Cathedral and in 1906, the Sacred Congregation of Rites made the Guild an Archconfraternity prima primaria enabling all the parish branches to be linked with it.
The Guild spread, and in 1934, Pope Pius XI enabled all Guilds of Altar Servers throughout the British Commonwealth to be affiliated with the Archconfraternity at Westminster.
The objectives of the Guild:
We are very proud that many of our children serve at Mass on a Sunday as well as ex-St Edmund’s pupils who continue to serve on a weekly basis.
Ministers of the Word
In proclaiming the word of God, readers exercise their responsibility in mediating the presence of Christ. God speaks to the congregation through them, and, the impact of God’s message will depend significantly on their conviction, their preparation, and their delivery.
The reader has responsibility for not simply reading the word, but assisting the congregation to hear the word. This requires the reader to be attentive to the congregation, and careful to allow for times of pause and silence as the congregation prepares to listen and, once the reading has been proclaimed, as it takes the word of God to heart.
We are incredibly lucky to have a team of readers from St Edmund’s School who help us understand the ‘Liturgy of the Word’ each week. We thank them for their service and commitment to this role – it is very difficult to read and project your voice to a church full of people particularly when there are so many younger members in the congregation.
Ministers of Music
The psalm and the gospel acclamation are integral and constitutive elements of the Liturgy of the Word. They are intended to be sung. Ministers of music exercise a liturgical function within each service and by their role help to add beauty and solemnity to the celebration.
Ministers of Music also have an important role in assisting the clergy and other liturgical ministers to develop confidence in using the chants provided in the Roman Missal for the dialogues, acclamations, intercessions and readings of the Liturgy of the Word.
At St Edmund’s we contribute by joining in with the singing but again we are incredibly lucky to have some of our families who play a larger part in the helping us to celebrate Mass through singing and music. If you feel you would like to help in this ministry, come along on a Sunday morning and join the Family Mass Choir.
Welcome Team
A servant's heart is the most important quality when practising this ministry. This team is made up of families who share their warmth and hospitality by giving a friendly smile to make people feel welcome at St Edmund’s Church.
Whoever you are, wherever you are from, whatever your background, you are welcome at St Edmund’s and the welcome team serve others by ensuring the congregation have the books and information needed to participate and share in the Mass with our whole congregation.
Thank you to the children from St Edmund’s and their families for carrying out this incredibly important ministry. You are the first people visitors see and you give that first impression of what our community is like – a happy place to be, a place where we can come to know God more closely.

pageCache.text:
Welcome from Parish Priest
Welcome to St Edmund’s Catholic Nursery and Primary School.
Our school and parish have always shared a very special bond, built on faith, care and community. This close relationship helps every child, from ages 3 to 11, grow in both learning and life. Parents consistently value the way our school and parish work hand in hand to create a safe, nurturing and faith-filled environment.
As a Catholic school, St Edmund’s helps children come to know and live the values of the Gospel. For Catholic families, this strengthens the faith nurtured at home and in the parish. For families of other faiths, and of none, it offers a warm, inclusive environment where many say they feel enriched and welcomed.
Staff, governors and pupils strive each day to live out our Catholic ethos. Together with the parish, we ensure that every child is encouraged to develop confidence, kindness and respect, qualities that will serve them throughout their lives.
I look forward to working together to give every child the very best start in life and faith.
God bless, Fr Jonathan
